question.text: Mr. Arjun Mehta, promoter-sponsor of Garuda Credit Opportunities AIF (Cat II), wants to transfer his sponsor units to his personal HUF after 18 months to save tax. Which statement reflects the SEBI restriction?

answer.text: Sponsor units are freely transferable after a 1-year lock-in.
Sponsor can transfer to any related party provided SEBI is notified.
Sponsor units can be transferred only to accredited investors after 2 years.
The sponsor's continuing interest cannot be withdrawn and remains locked-in until distributions to investors are completed in full; a transfer is possible only to another eligible sponsor/manager.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the sponsor/manager continuing interest CANNOT be withdrawn from the fund and remains locked-in until distributions to investors are completed. Sponsors are the first to commit and the last to be paid. A transfer to an HUF is not a permitted exit; only a transfer to another eligible sponsor who steps into the commitment is considered. The Trap: Option A invents a 1-year freeze. Option B assumes notification alone cures the lock-in. Option C mixes up accredited-investor rules with sponsor unit transferability. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B tests this lock-in from a distributor pitch angle. Compare with PMS (XXI-B) where no such sponsor lock-in exists — portfolio managers can withdraw proprietary capital at will. Manager's Pro-Tip: When onboarding a new GP to replace a departing sponsor, structure the substitution as a novation — not a sale — and seek SEBI prior approval for change of control. Investors often demand a re-approval right in the LPA for any sponsor transition.
